title: Animal Nutrition
standard_text: Nutrition in humans: the structure of the alimentary canal; ingestion, digestion (mechanical and chemical), absorption, assimilation and egestion; enzymes of digestion; the role of the liver and pancreas; homeostatic control of blood glucose; balanced diets and diet-related disorders. (summary of the senior secondary Biology curriculum, SSS 1; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 Biology worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): digestion and enzymes, digestion and absorption, breathing and digestion, enzymes in digestion and diet and health. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Digestion breaks large molecules into small soluble molecules.
key_sub: Villi give the small intestine a large surface area.
body_html:
How to think about it

Food passes from the mouth through the oesophagus, stomach, duodenum, ileum, colon and rectum. Mechanical digestion (teeth, churning) breaks food into smaller pieces; chemical digestion uses enzymes: amylase (starch), protease (protein) and lipase (fats). Bile from the liver emulsifies fats.

Digested food is absorbed through the villi of the ileum into the blood and lymph. The liver stores glycogen, makes bile and breaks down excess amino acids. A balanced diet contains carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water; poor diets lead to obesity, kwashiorkor or diabetes.

Example

Which enzyme digests starch?

Found in saliva

Answer: amylase

Example

What does bile do?

It is not an enzyme.

Answer: it emulsifies fats into small droplets

Common mistakes

  • Thinking bile is an enzyme.
  • Thinking food is absorbed in the stomach.
  • Mixing up digestion and absorption.
